title: How to add image descriptions
description: Image descriptions make >x< accessible to people with disabilities and help all readers understand your images. Learn how to add alt text to your posts on iOS, Android, and web.

runs: Image descriptions, also called alternative text, are an easy way to make >x< accessible to people with disabilities. Like posts, image descriptions must follow the

Describing what’s in your images benefits people who are blind, have low vision, use assistive technology, live in low-bandwidth areas, or want more context. Without descriptions, your readers won’t know what your images contain, or why they're important. This missing information prevents people from engaging with your post.
You can add image descriptions in four steps.
1. After uploading an image to a post, select the
button on the image. (“ALT” is the abbreviation for alternative text, which is the technical name for image description.)

items.alt: Screenshot of draft Tweet with the text “Morning espresso I must have.” With an uploaded image of a mug of espresso. The add image description button is located at the bottom of the image.

runs: 2. Enter a description of the image in the text box. The description for this image is: “A small white mug with a tiny loop handle, with a shot of deep brown espresso and a light brown crema on top. The mug sits on a small white saucer on a medium brown wooden table.” In the corner of the text box is the character count. We’ve used 178 characters of the 1,000 characters available.

items.alt: Screenshot of image description screen that shows uploaded image of espresso in mug, and text box with image description. The heading is “Write alt text.”

runs: 3. Select
. An ALT badge will appear in the corner of the image. The + symbol no longer appears on the badge now that the description has been added.

items.alt: Screenshot of draft Tweet with the text “Morning espresso I must have.” With uploaded image of a mug of espresso. The ALT badge is located at the bottom of the image.

runs: 4. Select
. The ALT badge appears on the image of the posted post. When someone selects the ALT badge, the image description appears on screen from the bottom up.

items.alt: Screenshot of the posted Tweet with the ALT badge on the image.
Screenshot of the posted Tweet with the image description appearing. “Image description” is the title, and a dismiss button comes after the description.
